correctness.rationale: For h<=1 strict Jensen gives unique all-equal dosing. For h>1, equal marginal utilities at any two unequal positive doses imply positive second derivative along their transfer, by the exact hyperbolic sine inequality, excluding such a pair in a local/global maximum. Every possible optimum is therefore equal on its positive support. The single-peaked g(t)=log(1+t^h)/t has a unique peak u_h, implying each adjacent k/k+1 objective crosses once in strictly ordered brackets; chaining rules out nonadjacent ties/skipped active counts. The stated theta_1 is solved algebraically. The included checker passed 52,569 exact-rational finite grid tests and 21,600 numeric random tests, plus 56 switch brackets; finite tests are supplemental, not a universal proof.

value.rationale: A natural coupled-resource independent-target model has nontrivial S-shaped cooperative dose response: optimal activation support does not merely change between all-to-one and spread-to-all, but necessarily uses every intervening integer support size in exact order, and no unequal positive split can ever win. The explicit sharp thresholds make an all-n, all-real-exponent allocation rule possible. This is a motivated structural boundary for interpreting independent Hill mechanisms and an exact benchmark for more realistic allocation models, not a renaming, trivial special case, or small numerical improvement. Model idealizations and unreviewed historical priority are explicitly distinguished from mathematical value.
